subs.title: Leibniz Rule, Integral Functions and Inequalities
Limit of a Sum and Reduction Formulae

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) be non-zero real numbers such that \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(1+\cos^8x)(ax^2+bx+c)dx=\int_0^2(1+\cos^8x)(ax^2+bx+c)dx\), then \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) has
questions.sol: Subtracting: \(\displaystyle\int_1^2(1+\cos^8x)(ax^2+bx+c)dx=0\). As \(1+\cos^8x>0\), the quadratic cannot keep one sign on \((1,2)\), so it vanishes there.

questions.q: The value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt{\cot x}}{\sqrt{\cot x}+\sqrt{\tan x}}dx\) is
For any integer \(n\), the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi e^{\cos^2x}\cos^3(2n+1)x\,dx\) has the value
questions.sol: Under \(x\to\pi-x\): \(\cos^2x\) is unchanged and \(\cos(2n+1)(\pi-x)=-\cos(2n+1)x\), so the integrand changes sign: \(I=-I\).

Let \(f:R\to R\) and \(g:R\to R\) be continuous functions. Then the value of integral \(\displaystyle\int_{-\frac\pi2}^{\frac\pi2}[f(x)+f(-x)][g(x)-g(-x)]dx\)
questions.sol: \(f(x)+f(-x)\) is even and \(g(x)-g(-x)\) is odd; their product is odd.

The value of \(\displaystyle\int_\pi^{2\pi}[2\sin x]dx\) where \([\cdot]\) represents the greatest integer function is

If \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x\cos^4t\,dt\) then \(g(x+\pi)\) equals
questions.sol: \(g(x+\pi)=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi+\int_\pi^{x+\pi}\), and since \(\cos^4t\) has period \(\pi\) the second integral equals \(g(x)\).

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a positive function. Let \(I_1=\displaystyle\int_{1-k}^kxf[x(1-x)]dx\), \(I_2=\displaystyle\int_{1-k}^kf[x(1-x)]dx\), where \(2k-1>0\), Then \(\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}\) is
questions.sol: Replacing \(x\) by \(1-x\) (the limits and \(x(1-x)\) are unchanged): \(I_1=\displaystyle\int(1-x)f[x(1-x)]dx=I_2-I_1\).

questions.q: If \(\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt=x+\int_x^1tf(t)dt\) then the value of \(f(1)\) is
Let \(f(x)=x-[x]\), for every real number \(x\), where \([x]\) is the integral part of \(x\), then \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1f(x)dx\) is
questions.sol: The fractional part has period \(1\) and \(\displaystyle\int_0^1x\,dx=\frac12\); over two periods the integral is \(1\).

questions.q: \(\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}\dfrac{dx}{1+\cos x}\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1{1+\cos x}=\dfrac12\sec^2\dfrac x2\), so the integral is \(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}8-\tan\dfrac\pi8=(\sqrt2+1)-(\sqrt2-1)\).

questions.q: If for a real number \(y\), \([y]\) is the greatest integer less than or equal to \(y\), then the value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}[2\sin x]dx\) is
questions.sol: \([2\sin x]\) is \(1\) on \(\left(\frac\pi2,\frac{5\pi}6\right)\), \(0\) on \(\left(\frac{5\pi}6,\pi\right)\), \(-1\) on \(\left(\pi,\frac{7\pi}6\right)\), \(-2\) on \(\left(\frac{7\pi}6,\frac{3\pi}2\right)\): \(\frac\pi3-\frac\pi6-\frac{2\pi}3\).

questions.q: Let \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt\), where \(f\) is such that \(\dfrac12\le f(t)\le1\) for \(t\in[0,1]\) and \(0\le f(t)\le\dfrac12\) for \(t\in[1,2]\) then \(g(2)\) satisfies the inequality,
questions.sol: \(\dfrac12\le\displaystyle\int_0^1f\le1\) and \(0\le\displaystyle\int_1^2f\le\dfrac12\), so \(\dfrac12\le g(2)\le\dfrac32\), which lies inside \([0,2)\).

questions.sol: \(f'(x)=2x\left[e^{-(x^2+1)^2}-e^{-x^4}\right]\); the bracket is negative, so \(f'>0\) for \(x<0\).

The value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt{\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}}dx\) is
\(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^0\left(x^3+3x^2+3x+3+(x+1)\cos(x+1)\right)dx\) is equal to
questions.sol: With \(u=x+1\): \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1\left(u^3+2+u\cos u\right)du\); the odd terms vanish, leaving \(2\cdot2\).

questions.q: If \(\displaystyle\int_{\sin x}^1t^2f(t)dt=1-\sin x\ \forall\ x\in\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right]\) then \(f\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\right)\) is
questions.sol: Differentiating: \(-\sin^2x\,f(\sin x)\cos x=-\cos x\), so \(f(\sin x)=\dfrac1{\sin^2x}\).

questions.q: \(\lim\limits_{x\to\frac\pi4}\dfrac{\displaystyle\int_2^{\sec^2x}f(t)dt}{x^2-\dfrac{\pi^2}{16}}\) equals
Let \(f\) be a non-negative function defined on the interval \([0,1]\). If \(\displaystyle\int_0^x\sqrt{1-(f'(t))^2}\,dt=\int_0^xf(t)dt\), \(0\le x\le1\), and \(f(0)=0\), then
questions.sol: Differentiating: \(\sqrt{1-f'^2}=f\), i.e. \(f'=\sqrt{1-f^2}\) with \(f(0)=0\), \(f\ge0\): \(f(x)=\sin x\). And \(\sin x<x\) for \(x>0\).

questions.q: The value of \(\displaystyle\int_{\sqrt{\ln2}}^{\sqrt{\ln3}}\dfrac{x\sin x^2}{\sin x^2+\sin(\ln6-x^2)}dx\) is
questions.sol: With \(t=x^2\): \(\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_{\ln2}^{\ln3}\dfrac{\sin t}{\sin t+\sin(\ln6-t)}dt\). Replacing \(t\) by \(\ln2+\ln3-t\) and adding, this integral is \(\dfrac12(\ln3-\ln2)\).

questions.q: The value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\left(x^2+\ln\dfrac{\pi+x}{\pi-x}\right)\cos x\,dx\) is
questions.sol: The logarithm term is odd. \(2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}x^2\cos x\,dx=2\left[x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x\right]_0^{\pi/2}=2\left(\dfrac{\pi^2}4-2\right)\).

questions.q: The following integral \(\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}(2\,\text{cosec}\,x)^{17}dx\) is equal to
questions.sol: Put \(\text{cosec}\,x+\cot x=e^u\); then \(\text{cosec}\,x-\cot x=e^{-u}\), \(2\,\text{cosec}\,x=e^u+e^{-u}\) and \(-\text{cosec}\,x\,dx=du\). Limits: \(x=\frac\pi4\to u=\log(1+\sqrt2)\), \(x=\frac\pi2\to u=0\). The integral becomes \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\log(1+\sqrt2)}2(e^u+e^{-u})^{16}du\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[0,2]\to R\) be a function which is continuous on \([0,2]\) and is differentiable on \((0,2)\) with \(f(0)=1\). Let \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^{x^2}f(\sqrt t)dt\) for \(x\in[0,2]\). If \(F'(x)=f'(x)\) for all \(x\in(0,2)\), then \(F(2)\) equals
The value of \(\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{x^2\cos x}{1+e^x}dx\) is equal to
questions.sol: Replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) and adding: \(2I=\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}x^2\cos x\,dx\), so \(I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}x^2\cos x\,dx=\dfrac{\pi^2}4-2\).

questions.q:
For positive integer \(n\), define \(f(n)=n+\dfrac{16+5n-3n^2}{4n+3n^2}+\dfrac{32+n-3n^2}{8n+3n^2}+\dfrac{48-3n-3n^2}{12n+3n^2}+\ldots+\dfrac{25n-7n^2}{7n^2}\)
Then, the value of \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}f(n)\) is equal to

Let \(f:(0,1)\to\mathbb R\) be the function defined as \(f(x)=\sqrt n\) if \(x\in\left[\dfrac1{n+1},\dfrac1n\right)\) where \(n\in\mathbb N\). Let \(g:(0,1)\to\mathbb R\) be a function such that \(\displaystyle\int_{x^2}^x\sqrt{\dfrac{1-t}t}dt<g(x)<2\sqrt x\) for all \(x\in(0,1)\). Then \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}f(x)g(x)\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1{n+1}\le x<\dfrac1n\) gives \(\sqrt{\dfrac n{n+1}}\le\sqrt xf(x)<1\), so \(\sqrt xf(x)\to1\). And \(\dfrac1{\sqrt x}\displaystyle\int_{x^2}^x\sqrt{\dfrac{1-t}t}dt\to2\) (L'Hôpital, or since the integrand is \(\approx t^{-1/2}\)), so \(\dfrac{g(x)}{\sqrt x}\to2\) by the sandwich theorem.

questions.q: Let \(S_n=\sum\limits_{k=1}^n\dfrac n{n^2+kn+k^2}\) and \(T_n=\sum\limits_{k=0}^{n-1}\dfrac n{n^2+kn+k^2}\), for \(n=1,2,3,\ldots\) Then,
questions.sol: Both are Riemann sums of the decreasing function \(\dfrac1{1+x+x^2}\) on \([0,1]\), whose integral is \(\dfrac\pi{3\sqrt3}\). \(S_n\) uses right end points (too small), \(T_n\) left end points (too large).

questions.q: If \(I_n=\displaystyle\int_{-\pi}^\pi\dfrac{\sin nx}{(1+\pi^x)\sin x}dx\), \(n=0,1,2,\ldots\), then
questions.sol: Replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) and adding: \(I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{\sin nx}{\sin x}dx\). \(I_{n+2}-I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi2\cos(n+1)x\,dx=0\). \(I_1=\pi\), \(I_2=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi2\cos x\,dx=0\); so odd ones are \(\pi\), even ones \(0\).

questions.q: The value (s) of \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{x^4(1-x)^4}{1+x^2}dx\) is (are)

The option(s) with the values of \(a\) and \(L\) that satisfy the following equation is(are) \(\dfrac{\displaystyle\int_0^{4\pi}e^t(\sin^6at+\cos^4at)dt}{\displaystyle\int_0^\pi e^t(\sin^6at+\cos^4at)dt}=L\)?
questions.sol: For \(a=2\) or \(4\), \(\sin^6at+\cos^4at\) has period \(\pi\). Shifting by \(k\pi\): \(\displaystyle\int_{k\pi}^{(k+1)\pi}=e^{k\pi}\int_0^\pi\). So \(L=1+e^\pi+e^{2\pi}+e^{3\pi}=\dfrac{e^{4\pi}-1}{e^\pi-1}\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=7\tan^8x+7\tan^6x-3\tan^4x-3\tan^2x\) for all \(x\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then the correct expression(s) is(are)
questions.sol: \(f(x)=(7\tan^6x-3\tan^2x)\sec^2x=\dfrac d{dx}\left(\tan^7x-\tan^3x\right)\), which vanishes at \(0\) and \(\frac\pi4\): (b). By parts, \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}xf=-\int_0^{\pi/4}(\tan^7x-\tan^3x)dx=-\int_0^1t^3(t^2-1)dt=\dfrac14-\dfrac16\).

questions.q: Let \(f'(x)=\dfrac{192x^3}{2+\sin^4\pi x}\) for all \(x\in R\) with \(f\left(\dfrac12\right)=0\). If \(m\le\displaystyle\int_{1/2}^1f(x)dx\le M\), then the possible values of \(m\) and \(M\) are
questions.sol: \(64x^3\le f'(x)\le96x^3\), so \(16x^4-1\le f(x)\le24x^4-\dfrac32\) on \(\left[\frac12,1\right]\). Integrating: \(2.6\le\displaystyle\int_{1/2}^1f\le3.9\), which lies in \([1,12]\) only.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(\dfrac{n^n(x+n)\left(x+\dfrac n2\right)\ldots\left(x+\dfrac nn\right)}{n!(x^2+n^2)\left(x^2+\dfrac{n^2}4\right)\ldots\left(x^2+\dfrac{n^2}{n^2}\right)}\right)^{\frac xn}\), for all \(x>0\). Then
questions.sol: The \(k\)th factor is \(\dfrac{1+x\frac kn}{1+x^2\frac{k^2}{n^2}}\), so \(\ln f(x)=x\displaystyle\int_0^1\ln\dfrac{1+xt}{1+x^2t^2}dt=\int_0^x\ln\dfrac{1+u}{1+u^2}du\) and \(\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}=\ln\dfrac{1+x}{1+x^2}\): positive on \((0,1)\), negative for \(x>1\), and decreasing there (\(\ln\frac4{10}<\ln\frac35\)).

questions.q: If \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_{\sin x}^{\sin2x}\sin^{-1}(t)dt\), then
questions.sol: \(g'(x)=2\cos2x\,\sin^{-1}(\sin2x)-\cos x\,\sin^{-1}(\sin x)\). At \(x=\pm\dfrac\pi2\): \(\sin2x=0\) and \(\cos x=0\), so \(g'\left(\pm\dfrac\pi2\right)=0\). No option is correct — this question was treated as a bonus.

questions.q: If \(I=\sum\limits_{k=1}^{98}\displaystyle\int_k^{k+1}\dfrac{k+1}{x(x+1)}dx\), then
Which of the following inequalities is/are TRUE?
Consider the equation \(\displaystyle\int_1^e\dfrac{(\log_ex)^{1/2}}{x\left(a-(\log_ex)^{3/2}\right)^2}dx=1\), \(a\in(-\infty,0)\cup(1,\infty)\). Which of the following statements is/are true ?
opts: An integer \(a\) satisfies the above equation
An irrational number \(a\) satisfies the above equation
More than one \(a\) satisfy the above equation
questions.sol: With \(t=(\log_ex)^{3/2}\): \(\dfrac23\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{dt}{(a-t)^2}=\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac1{a(a-1)}=1\), so \(3a^2-3a-2=0\), \(a=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{33}}6\): both irrational, one below \(0\) and one above \(1\).

questions.q: Show that : \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(\dfrac1{n+1}+\dfrac1{n+2}+\ldots+\dfrac1{6n}\right)=\log6\)

Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(tx+1-x)^ndx\) where \(n\) is a positive integer and \(t\) is a parameter independent of \(x\). Hence show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^1x^k(1-x)^{n-k}dx=\left[{}^nC_k(n+1)\right]^{-1}\) for \(k=0,1,2,\ldots,n\)
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\left((t-1)x+1\right)^ndx=\left[\dfrac{((t-1)x+1)^{n+1}}{(n+1)(t-1)}\right]_0^1=\dfrac{t^{n+1}-1}{(n+1)(t-1)}\). Expanding the integrand as \(\sum{}^nC_kt^kx^k(1-x)^{n-k}\) and comparing the coefficients of \(t^k\) with \(\dfrac1{n+1}\): \({}^nC_k\displaystyle\int_0^1x^k(1-x)^{n-k}dx=\dfrac1{n+1}\).

questions.q: Show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi xf(\sin x)dx=\dfrac\pi2\int_0^\pi f(\sin x)dx\)
Find the value of \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{3/2}|x\sin\pi x|dx\)
questions.sol: \(x\sin\pi x\ge0\) on \([-1,1]\) and \(\le0\) on \(\left[1,\frac32\right]\). \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1x\sin\pi x\,dx=\dfrac2\pi\) and \(-\displaystyle\int_1^{3/2}x\sin\pi x\,dx=\dfrac1\pi+\dfrac1{\pi^2}\) (by parts).

questions.q: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{9+16\sin2x}dx\)
questions.sol: With \(t=\sin x-\cos x\): \(\sin2x=1-t^2\) and \(dt=(\cos x+\sin x)dx\): \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^0\dfrac{dt}{25-16t^2}=\dfrac1{40}\left[\log\dfrac{5+4t}{5-4t}\right]_{-1}^0=\dfrac1{40}\log9\).

questions.q: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}\dfrac{x\sin^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx\)

Given a function \(f(x)\) such that
(i) It is integrable over every interval on the real line and
(ii) \(f(t+x)=f(x)\) for every \(x\) and a real \(t\) then show that the integral \(\displaystyle\int_a^{a+t}f(x)dx\) is independent of \(a\)
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int_a^{a+t}=\int_a^0+\int_0^t+\int_t^{a+t}\), and with \(x=u+t\) the last integral is \(\displaystyle\int_0^af(u+t)du=\int_0^af(u)du\), which cancels the first. So the value is \(\displaystyle\int_0^tf(x)dx\).

questions.q: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{x\sin x\cos x\,dx}{\cos^4x+\sin^4x}\)
Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{x\,dx}{1+\cos\alpha\sin x}\), \(0<\alpha<\pi\)
Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\log\left[\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x}\right]dx\)
questions.sol: By parts: \(\left[x\log(\cdot)\right]_0^1=\log\sqrt2\), and \(\dfrac d{dx}\log\left(\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{1+x}\right)=-\dfrac{1-\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}}\). So the remaining part is \(\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt{1-x^2}}-1\right)dx=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac\pi2-1\right)\).

questions.q: If \(f\) and \(g\) are continuous functions on \((0,a)\) satisfying \(f(x)=f(a-x)\) and \(g(x)+g(a-x)=2\) then show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^af(x)g(x)dx=\int_0^af(x)dx\)
Show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac\pi2}f(\sin2x)\sin x\,dx=\sqrt2\int_0^{\frac\pi4}f(\cos2x)\cos x\,dx\)
questions.sol: With \(x\to\frac\pi2-x\): \(I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}f(\sin2x)\cos x\,dx\). Adding: \(2I=\sqrt2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}f(\sin2x)\cos\left(x-\dfrac\pi4\right)dx\). With \(u=x-\frac\pi4\): \(\sqrt2\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}f(\cos2u)\cos u\,du=2\sqrt2\int_0^{\pi/4}f(\cos2u)\cos u\,du\).

questions.q: If '\(f\)' is a continuous function with \(\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt\to\infty\) as \(|x|\to\infty\), then show that every line \(y=mx\) intersects the curve \(y^2+\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt=2\)
questions.sol: Substituting \(y=mx\): \(g(x)=m^2x^2+\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt-2\) is continuous with \(g(0)=-2<0\) and \(g(x)\to\infty\) as \(|x|\to\infty\). By the intermediate value theorem \(g\) has a root.

questions.q: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{x\sin(2x)\sin\left(\dfrac\pi2\cos x\right)}{2x-\pi}dx\)
questions.sol: With \(x\to\pi-x\) and adding: \(2I=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\sin2x\sin\left(\dfrac\pi2\cos x\right)dx\). Put \(t=\frac\pi2\cos x\): \(\sin2x\,dx=-\dfrac8{\pi^2}t\,dt\), giving \(\dfrac8{\pi^2}\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}t\sin t\,dt=\dfrac{16}{\pi^2}\).

questions.q: A cubic \(f(x)\) vanishes at \(x=-2\) and has relative minimum/maximum at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1/3\) if \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1f(x)dx=\dfrac{14}3\), find the cubic \(f(x)\).
Determine a positive integer \(n\le5\), such that \(\displaystyle\int_0^1e^x(x-1)^ndx=16-6e\)
Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_2^3\dfrac{2x^5+x^4-2x^3+2x^2+1}{(x^2+1)(x^4-1)}dx\)
If \(n\) is a positive integer and \(0\le v<\pi\) then show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^{n\pi+v}|\sin x|dx=2n+1-\cos v\)
questions.sol: \(|\sin x|\) has period \(\pi\) with \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\sin x\,dx=2\), so \(\displaystyle\int_0^{n\pi}=2n\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{n\pi}^{n\pi+v}|\sin x|dx=\int_0^v\sin u\,du=1-\cos v\).

questions.q: Evaluate \(I=\displaystyle\int_{-1/\sqrt3}^{1/\sqrt3}\dfrac{x^4}{1-x^4}\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)dx\)
Using mathematical induction, for \(I_m=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{1-\cos mx}{1-\cos x}dx\) prove that \(I_m=m\pi\), \(m=0,1,2,\ldots\)
Determine the value of \(\displaystyle\int_{-\pi}^\pi\dfrac{2x(1+\sin x)}{1+\cos^2x}dx\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{2x}{1+\cos^2x}\) is odd. The rest is \(4\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{x\sin x}{1+\cos^2x}dx=4\cdot\dfrac\pi2\int_0^\pi\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2x}dx=2\pi\cdot\dfrac\pi2\).

questions.q: Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\ln(1+\tan x)dx\)
Prove that \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac1{1-x+x^2}\right)dx=2\int_0^1\tan^{-1}x\,dx\). Hence or otherwise, evaluate the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\tan^{-1}(1-x+x^2)dx\).
Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{e^{\cos x}}{e^{\cos x}+e^{-\cos x}}dx\)
For \(x>0\), let \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_1^x\dfrac{\ln t}{1+t}dt\), find the function \(f(x)+f\left(\dfrac1x\right)\) and show that \(f(e)+f\left(\dfrac1e\right)=1/2\). Here \(\ln(t)=\log t\).
If the function \(f:[0,4]\to R\) is differentiable, then Show that \(\displaystyle\int_0^4f(t)dt=2\left[\alpha f(\alpha^2)+\beta f(\beta^2)\right]\) for some \(0<\alpha,\beta<2\)
questions.sol: Let \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^{x^2}f(t)dt\), \(F'(x)=2xf(x^2)\). By the mean value theorem on \([0,1]\) and \([1,2]\): \(F(1)-F(0)=2\alpha f(\alpha^2)\) and \(F(2)-F(1)=2\beta f(\beta^2)\) with \(0<\alpha<1<\beta<2\). Adding gives \(F(2)=\displaystyle\int_0^4f(t)dt\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)\) is an even function, then prove that \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac\pi2}f(\cos2x)\cos x\,dx=\sqrt2\int_0^{\frac\pi4}f(\sin2x)\cos x\,dx\)
questions.sol: With \(x\to\frac\pi2-x\) and \(f\) even: \(I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}f(\cos2x)\sin x\,dx\). Adding: \(2I=\sqrt2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}f(\cos2x)\cos\left(x-\dfrac\pi4\right)dx\); with \(u=x-\frac\pi4\), \(\cos2x=-\sin2u\): \(\sqrt2\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}f(\sin2u)\cos u\,du=2\sqrt2\int_0^{\pi/4}f(\sin2u)\cos u\,du\).

questions.q: If \(y(x)=\displaystyle\int_{\pi^2/16}^{x^2}\dfrac{\cos x\cdot\cos\sqrt\theta}{1+\sin^2\sqrt\theta}d\theta\), find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x=\pi\).
Evaluate \(\displaystyle\int_{-\frac\pi3}^{\frac\pi3}\dfrac{\pi+4x^3}{2-\cos\left(|x|+\dfrac\pi3\right)}dx\)
questions.sol: The \(x^3\) part is odd. \(2\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/3}\dfrac{dx}{2-\cos\left(x+\frac\pi3\right)}\); with \(t=\tan\frac12\left(x+\frac\pi3\right)\) from \(\frac1{\sqrt3}\) to \(\sqrt3\): \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2\,dt}{1+3t^2}=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\left[\tan^{-1}3-\tan^{-1}1\right]\).

questions.q: Evaluate \(I=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi e^{|\cos x|}\left(2\sin\left(\dfrac12\cos x\right)+3\cos\left(\dfrac12\cos x\right)\right)\sin x\,dx\)
questions.sol: Under \(x\to\pi-x\) the \(\sin\left(\frac12\cos x\right)\) term changes sign (integral \(0\)) and the other is unchanged: \(I=6\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}e^{\cos x}\cos\left(\dfrac12\cos x\right)\sin x\,dx=6\int_0^1e^t\cos\dfrac t2dt=6\cdot\dfrac45\left[e^t\left(\cos\dfrac t2+\dfrac12\sin\dfrac t2\right)\right]_0^1\).

questions.sol: \(R_1\to R_1-\sec x\,R_3\) makes the first row \((0,\ 0,\ \sec^2x+\cot x\,\text{cosec}\,x-\cos x)\), so \(f=(\sec^2x+\cot x\,\text{cosec}\,x-\cos x)(\cos^4x-\cos^2x)=-\sin^2x-\cos^5x\). The integral is \(-\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac8{15}\).

(A) If \(\vec a=\hat j+\sqrt3\hat k\), \(\vec b=-\hat j+\sqrt3\hat k\) and \(\vec c=2\sqrt3\hat k\) form a triangle, then the internal angle of the triangle between \(\vec a\) and \(\vec b\) is(p) \(\pi/6\)
(B) If \(\displaystyle\int_a^b(f(x)-3x)dx=a^2-b^2\), then the value of \(f\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)\) is(q) \(2\pi/3\)
(C) The value of \(\dfrac{\pi^2}{\ln3}\displaystyle\int_{7/6}^{5/6}\sec(\pi x)dx\) is(r) \(\pi/3\)
(D) The maximum value of \(\left|\text{Arg}\left(\dfrac1{1-z}\right)\right|\) for \(|z|=1\), \(z\ne1\) is given by(s) \(\pi\)
(t) \(\pi/2\)
questions.sol: (A) \(\vec a+\vec b=\vec c\), so \(\vec a,\vec b\) are placed head to tail; the angle between the vectors is \(\frac\pi3\) (\(\cos=\frac24\)), so the internal angle is \(\pi-\frac\pi3\). (B) \(\displaystyle\int_a^bf=\frac{b^2-a^2}2\) for all \(a,b\) gives \(f(x)=x\). (C) \(\dfrac{\pi}{\ln3}\left[\ln|\sec\pi x+\tan\pi x|\right]_{7/6}^{5/6}=\dfrac\pi{\ln3}\left(\ln\sqrt3+\ln\sqrt3\right)=\pi\). (D) \(\dfrac1{1-z}\) has real part \(\frac12\), so its argument lies in \(\left(-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right)\) and approaches \(\frac\pi2\).

Let \(\psi_1:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), \(\psi_2:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), be functions such that \(f(0)=g(0)=0\), \(\psi_1(x)=e^{-x}+x\), \(x\ge0\), \(\psi_2(x)=x^2-2x-2e^{-x}+2\), \(x\ge0\), \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-x}^x(|t|-t^2)e^{-t^2}dt\), \(x>0\) and \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^{x^2}\sqrt te^{-t}dt\), \(x>0\).
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
opts: For every \(x>1\), there exists an \(\alpha\in(1,x)\) such that \(\psi_1(x)=1+\alpha x\)
For every \(x>0\), there exists a \(\beta\in(0,x)\) such that \(\psi_2(x)=2x(\psi_1(\beta)-1)\)
\(f\) is an increasing function on the interval \(\left[0,\dfrac32\right]\)
questions.sol: \(\psi_2'(x)=2x-2+2e^{-x}=2(\psi_1(x)-1)\) and \(\psi_2(0)=0\); the mean value theorem gives \(\psi_2(x)=x\psi_2'(\beta)\): (c). Also \(f(x)=2\displaystyle\int_0^x(t-t^2)e^{-t^2}dt\) and \(g(x)=2\displaystyle\int_0^xu^2e^{-u^2}du\), so \(f+g=1-e^{-x^2}\), which is \(\frac23\) at \(\sqrt{\ln3}\); \(f'=2(x-x^2)e^{-x^2}<0\) for \(x>1\); and \(\psi_1(x)-1=x+e^{-x}-1<x\) rules out (b).

The lower bound gives \(g\ge\frac23x^3-\frac25x^5\), so \(f=1-e^{-x^2}-g\le1-e^{-x^2}-\frac23x^3+\frac25x^5\): (c) is false. \(\psi_1,\psi_2\) are increasing from \(\psi_1(0)=1\), \(\psi_2(0)=0\): (a), (b) false.

Let \(f:R\to R\) be a continuous odd function, which vanishes exactly at one point and \(f(1)=\dfrac12\). Suppose that \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^xf(t)dt\) for all \(x\in[-1,2]\) and \(G(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^xt|f(f(t))|dt\) for all \(x\in[-1,2]\). If \(\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{F(x)}{G(x)}=\dfrac1{14}\), then the value of \(f\left(\dfrac12\right)\) is
questions.sol: Both integrands are odd, so \(F(1)=G(1)=0\). L'Hôpital: \(\dfrac{f(1)}{1\cdot|f(f(1))|}=\dfrac{1/2}{\left|f\left(\frac12\right)\right|}=\dfrac1{14}\). \(f\) vanishes only at \(0\) and \(f(1)>0\), so \(f\left(\frac12\right)=7\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be a differentiable function such that \(f(0)=0\), \(f\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=3\) and \(f'(0)=1\). If \(g(x)=\displaystyle\int_x^{\pi/2}[f'(t)\text{cosec}\,t-\cot t\,\text{cosec}\,t\,f(t)]dt\) for \(x\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right]\), then \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}g(x)=\) _________.
questions.sol: The integrand is \(\dfrac d{dt}\left[f(t)\text{cosec}\,t\right]\), so \(g(x)=3-\dfrac{f(x)}{\sin x}\to3-f'(0)\).

questions.q: For each positive integer \(n\), let \(y_n=\dfrac1n((n+1)(n+2)\ldots(n+n))^{\frac1n}\). For \(x\in\mathbb R\), let \([x]\) be the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\). If \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}y_n=L\), then the value of \([L]\) is ___ .
The value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}\dfrac{1+\sqrt3}{\left((x+1)^2(1-x)^6\right)^{1/4}}dx\) is _______.

The value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{3\sqrt{\cos\theta}}{(\sqrt{\cos\theta}+\sqrt{\sin\theta})^5}d\theta\) equals ____.

Let \(f:R\to R\) be a differentiable function such that its derivative \(f'\) is continuous and \(f(\pi)=-6\). If \(F:[0,\pi]\to R\) is defined by \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt\), and if \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi(f'(x)+F(x))\cos x\,dx=2\), then the value of \(f(0)\) is _____.
questions.sol: By parts: \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi f'\cos x=-f(\pi)-f(0)+\int_0^\pi f\sin x\) and \(\displaystyle\int_0^\pi F\cos x=-\int_0^\pi f\sin x\). Sum: \(6-f(0)=2\).

For any real number \(x\), let \([x]\) denote the largest integer less than or equal to \(x\). If \(I=\displaystyle\int_0^{10}\left[\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x+1}}\right]dx\), then the value of \(9I\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x+1}}\) increases; it reaches \(1,2,3\) at \(x=\frac19,\frac23,9\) and stays below \(\sqrt{10}\). \(I=\left(\frac23-\frac19\right)+2\left(9-\frac23\right)+3(10-9)=\dfrac{182}9\).

questions.q: The greatest integer less than or equal to \(\displaystyle\int_1^2\log_2(x^3+1)dx+\int_1^{\log_29}(2^x-1)^{1/3}dx\) is _____.
questions.sol: \(y=\log_2(x^3+1)\) and \(x=(2^y-1)^{1/3}\) are inverse functions, with \(y(1)=1\), \(y(2)=\log_29\). So the sum is \(2\log_29-1\cdot1\approx5.34\).

The value of \(\dfrac{16}{\pi^3}\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}f(x)g(x)dx\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}fg=\dfrac12\int_0^{\pi/2}g\), and \(y=g(x)\) is the upper semicircle of radius \(\frac\pi4\) centred at \(\left(\frac\pi4,0\right)\), of area \(\dfrac{\pi^3}{32}\). Value \(\dfrac{16}{\pi^3}\cdot\dfrac{\pi^3}{64}\).

questions.q:
If \(\alpha=\displaystyle\int_{\frac12}^2\dfrac{\tan^{-1}x}{2x^2-3x+2}dx\), then the value of \(\sqrt7\tan\left(\dfrac{2\alpha\sqrt7}\pi\right)\) is ______.
(Here, the inverse trigonometric function \(\tan^{-1}x\) assumes values in \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\).)
questions.sol: \(x\to\dfrac1x\) gives the same integral with \(\tan^{-1}\dfrac1x\); adding, \(2\alpha=\dfrac\pi2\displaystyle\int_{\frac12}^2\dfrac{dx}{2x^2-3x+2}=\dfrac\pi2\cdot\dfrac2{\sqrt7}\left[\tan^{-1}\dfrac{4x-3}{\sqrt7}\right]_{\frac12}^2\). So \(\dfrac{2\alpha\sqrt7}\pi=\tan^{-1}\dfrac5{\sqrt7}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac1{\sqrt7}\), whose tangent is \(\dfrac{6/\sqrt7}{1-5/7}=3\sqrt7\).

questions.sol: Replacing \(x\) by \(2-x\): \(\dfrac1{3^{2-x}+3}=\dfrac{3^x}{3(3^x+3)}\). Adding the two forms, the integrand is \(\dfrac13\): \(2I=\dfrac23\).
